acceptance_criteria: The probe returns both projected endpoint tip speeds (recorded input and braking-box input) and the endpoint tip position difference for the same saved state and 0.01 s horizon.

If the endpoint speed difference is at numerical resolution (indistinguishable), record explicitly that this check cannot separate local braking-headroom from an already-braking-limited input, and make no causal statement.

If the endpoint speed difference is nonzero, report it only as a bounded local 10 ms endpoint difference; do not present it as an explanation of the sustained late-window speed/position error or as a dominant settling cause.
discriminating_observations: Projected endpoint tip speed under held recorded applied tension versus under the instantaneous braking-box input over 0.01 s; a materially lower braking-box endpoint speed supports H-local-braking-available, a resolution-level difference supports H-local-input-not-different.
Projected endpoint tip position difference between the two inputs, which indicates whether the local input change moves the tip on the 10 ms timescale at all.

Context only (already recorded, not evidence of this probe's outcome): sampled late-window measured tip speeds remain far above 0.02 m/s (0.22577-1.32948 m/s), late_motion speed 0.86187 m/s at t=0.30 s, and predicted-versus-measured tip velocity difference norms of 0.02232-0.02432 m/s with projection residuals 0.66-2.92 rad/m.
fixed_conditions: model.gvs@1.0.0 with implicit_euler integration at 0.002 s step and fixed 0.01 s horizon
saved projected state and recorded applied input of controller update 30 bound by the host from the inventory controller file; no state vector or input copied here
identical saved state, previous input, horizon and model for both compared inputs; exactly one factor changed (recorded applied tension versus instantaneous braking-box input)
world frame for tip vectors; projected GVS coordinates for state; this is a 10 ms local endpoint probe, not a closed-loop or full-backend replay
hypotheses: H-local-braking-available: holding the recorded applied tension of update 30 over the fixed 0.01 s horizon yields a projected endpoint tip speed that stays far above the recorded settling scale (0.02 m/s), while an instantaneous braking-box input from the same saved projected state yields a materially lower endpoint tip speed — i.e. locally available braking authority is not used by the recorded plan.

H-local-input-not-different: holding the recorded applied tension and the instantaneous braking-box input from the same saved projected state produce endpoint tip speeds that differ by no more than numerical resolution (and nearly identical endpoint position), so the recorded input is already at or near the local braking limit and this 10 ms probe cannot separate input choice from any other factor.

H-nonseparable: even if a nonzero endpoint difference appears, objective weighting, seed/shallow-iterate plan selection, effective-horizon effects and projected-GVS-versus-backend model mismatch all predict the same direction of endpoint difference and cannot be separated by this single local probe; no dominant settling cause is claimed either way.
local_question: At the saved projected state of controller update 30 (late settling window, controller start 0.30 s, matched endpoint 0.31 s, sampled measured tip speed 1.32948 m/s), does an instantaneous braking-box tension over the fixed 0.01 s horizon produce a different projected tip endpoint speed and position than holding the update's recorded applied tension — and by how much?
metrics: projected endpoint tip speed under the recorded applied input (m/s)
projected endpoint tip speed under the instantaneous braking-box input (m/s)
difference in projected endpoint tip speed between the two inputs (m/s)
projected endpoint tip position difference between the two inputs (m)
unresolved: This probe cannot separate objective weighting, seed/shallow-iterate plan selection, effective-horizon effects and projected-GVS-versus-backend model mismatch when they predict the same 10 ms endpoint difference; it identifies no dominant settling cause.

A 10 ms projected-model endpoint probe cannot explain the entire settling failure (late_max_speed_m_s 1.581 vs 0.02 m/s and late_max_error_m 0.05814 vs 0.01 m over the 0.05 s window), regardless of outcome.

Tension/force-limit saturation as a braking-authority limit is not resolvable here: per-update force_limit_saturated and tension_tracking_error_n were not read in this context, though source.force_limits is retained at 8.0 N on all six channels.
Whether applied plans were seed iterates or converged-but-poor solutions is not computable: source.historical_full_plans (control_snapshots.json) is not retained.

Closed-loop counterfactual replay and causal attribution are retained_unavailable; unread coverage in this context includes one-step predictions for updates 0-18, backend motion before about 0.29 s, and raw saved projected states.
